sub_theme: Materials: What Are Toys Made Of?

lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Reading About Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve information from a simple non-fiction text about materials.
success_criteria: I can find a fact in a non-fiction text.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss the difference between fiction and non-fiction.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a simple non-fiction text about materials, demonstrating how to find facts.
lessons.independent_task: Children read a non-fiction extract about materials and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: What material does the text mention?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact in a non-fiction book at home.

lessons.title: Place Value: Tens and Ones (Introduction)
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent numbers to 20 using tens and ones.
success_criteria: I can show a number using tens and ones.
I can say how many tens and ones make a number.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap counting in tens and ones informally.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model representing numbers 11-20 as '1 ten and some ones' using base-10 blocks.
lessons.independent_task: Children represent given numbers using tens and ones blocks, recording their representations.
key_questions: How many tens and ones make 15?
Can you show me 18 using blocks?

differentiation.support: Focus on numbers 11-15 with concrete blocks

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early place value understanding — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Practise representing numbers with any small objects grouped in 10s.

lessons.title: Naming and Sorting Materials Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and sort a range of materials confidently.
success_criteria: I can name 6 different materials.
I can sort objects by material.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap materials learned in Week 1 and Week 3.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Consolidate material names (wood, plastic, metal, glass, fabric, paper, rubber) with examples.
lessons.independent_task: Children sort a larger collection of objects by material, recording in a table.
resources_needed: Collection of objects made from varied materials
key_questions: What material is this?
Can you sort these into groups?
lessons.assessment_notes: Baseline consolidation check before deeper property work this week — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap of all materials known so far.
lessons.home_link: Find and name materials of 5 objects at home.

lessons.title: Describing Material Properties with Adjectives
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use adjectives to describe material properties.
success_criteria: I can use an adjective to describe a material.
I can write a sentence using it.
lessons.starter_activity: Feel different material samples and think of describing words.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model using adjectives (hard, soft, rough, smooth, shiny, dull) to describe materials in sentences.
lessons.independent_task: Children write sentences describing material properties using adjectives.
key_questions: What adjective describes this material?
Can you write a sentence using it?

differentiation.greater_depth: Use 2+ adjectives per sentence with varied vocabulary

lessons.assessment_notes: Note descriptive vocabulary and sentence writing — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share descriptive sentences with a partner.
lessons.home_link: Describe a material at home using an adjective.

lessons.title: Introduction to Halves
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find half of a shape or small quantity.
success_criteria: I can find half of a shape by folding.
I can find half of a small number of objects.
lessons.starter_activity: Fold a piece of paper in half and discuss equal parts.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding half of shapes (folding) and half of small quantities (sharing counters into 2 equal groups).
lessons.independent_task: Children find half of given shapes and quantities, recording their answers.
key_questions: What is half of this shape?
What is half of 8 counters?

differentiation.support: Find half of quantities up to 6 with counters
differentiation.greater_depth: Find half of quantities up to 20 and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early fraction understanding — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find half of a small group of objects at home.

lessons.title: Testing Materials: Bendy or Stiff?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to test and classify materials as bendy or stiff.
success_criteria: I can predict if a material is bendy or stiff.
I can test and record my results.
lessons.starter_activity: Predict which materials will bend easily.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model gently testing material samples for flexibility, recording results in a simple table.
lessons.independent_task: Children test a range of materials for bendiness, recording predictions and results.
key_questions: Was your prediction correct?
Which material was stiffest?

differentiation.greater_depth: Test 6+ materials and rank by flexibility

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skill: predicting and testing — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap bendy vs stiff materials found.
lessons.home_link: Test if a material at home is bendy or stiff (safely, with permission).

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Material-Themed Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read material-themed words containing Phase 5 graphemes.
success_criteria: I can blend and read material words.
I can read a sentence about materials.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Introduce/reinforce a grapheme, blending material-themed words (e.g. 'wood', 'glass', 'metal').
lessons.independent_task: Children read material-themed word and sentence cards, recording tricky ones.
key_questions: Can you blend this word?
Can you read this sentence?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics application to themed vocabulary — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading material words over the week.

lessons.title: Introduction to Quarters
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to find a quarter of a shape or small quantity.
success_criteria: I can find a quarter of a shape by folding.
I can find a quarter of a small number of objects.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model finding a quarter of shapes (folding in half twice) and quantities (sharing into 4 equal groups).
lessons.independent_task: Children find a quarter of given shapes and quantities, recording their answers.
key_questions: What is a quarter of this shape?
What is a quarter of 12 counters?

differentiation.support: Find a quarter of quantities up to 8 with counters
differentiation.greater_depth: Find a quarter of quantities up to 20 and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record early fraction understanding (quarters) — evidence for MATHS.N4.
lessons.home_link: Find a quarter of a small group of objects at home.

lessons.title: Choosing the Best Material for a Toy Boat
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to choose a suitable material for a purpose based on its properties.
success_criteria: I can choose a material for a toy boat.
I can explain why it's suitable.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap floating and sinking from earlier learning if covered, or predict which materials float.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what properties a good toy boat material needs (waterproof, floats, light).
lessons.independent_task: Children test a few materials for floating, then choose and justify the best material for a toy boat.
key_questions: Does this material float?
Why would this be good for a toy boat?

differentiation.support: Adult supports testing and simple justification
differentiation.greater_depth: Justify choice using multiple properties (waterproof, light, floats)

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of material property knowledge to a design purpose — evidence for SCI.MAT, linking towards simple DT thinking.
lessons.plenary: Recap the best material choices for a toy boat.
lessons.home_link: Predict which household objects would float in the bath.

lessons.title: Writing Instructions: How to Test a Material
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write simple instructions in the correct order.
success_criteria: I can write instructions using sequencing words.
I can put my instructions in the right order.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing simple instructions for testing a material (e.g. testing if it's waterproof).
lessons.independent_task: Children write 3-4 step instructions for testing a material property, using sequencing words.
key_questions: What is the first step?
What comes next?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note instructional writing and sequencing skill — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.plenary: Share instructions with a partner and follow them.
lessons.home_link: Write instructions for a simple task at home.

lessons.title: Place Value Recap and Application
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply tens and ones understanding to compare numbers.
success_criteria: I can represent a number using tens and ones.
I can say which of two numbers is bigger using place value.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap tens and ones from Monday.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing two numbers using tens and ones representations.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare pairs of numbers using base-10 blocks, recording which is bigger/smaller.
key_questions: Which number has more tens?
Which number is bigger?

differentiation.support: Compare numbers within 20 with concrete blocks
differentiation.greater_depth: Compare numbers within 50 and explain reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Record place value application to comparison — evidence for MATHS.N1.
lessons.home_link: Compare two numbers at home using tens and ones reasoning.

lessons.title: Materials Investigation: Which Material Is Best for a Raincoat?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to plan and carry out a simple fair test on material suitability.
success_criteria: I can test a material for waterproofness.
I can say if it would be good for a raincoat.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss what a raincoat needs to do.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model a simple fair test: dropping water on different material samples and observing.
lessons.independent_task: Children carry out the fair test on 3-4 materials, recording results and concluding which is best for a raincoat.
key_questions: What happened when water touched this material?
Which material would make the best raincoat?

differentiation.support: Adult supports testing and simple conclusion
differentiation.greater_depth: Test 5+ materials and write a reasoned conclusion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note fair testing skill and conclusion-drawing — evidence for SCI.MAT, a key working scientifically skill.
lessons.plenary: Recap the best raincoat material found through testing.
lessons.home_link: Check what material your own raincoat (or umbrella) is made from.

lessons.title: Materials Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about a materials-themed text.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a short materials-themed passage, modelling both retrieval and simple inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What material is mentioned?
Why do you think that material was chosen?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing
differentiation.greater_depth: Answer inference questions with full-sentence reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Read a non-fiction text together and ask an inference question.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Place Value and Fractions
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply place value and simple fraction skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can represent numbers using tens and ones.
I can find half and a quarter of a shape or quantity.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of tens and ones, halves, and quarters.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 3 stations: tens and ones representation, finding halves, finding quarters.
key_questions: How many tens and ones?
What is half/a quarter of this?
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 5 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N1/N4.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining all three skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising halves and quarters over the weekend.

lessons.title: Materials Topic Recap and Celebration
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key material properties and testing skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can name 3 material properties.
I can recall how we tested them.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering material properties (bendy, waterproof, strong) and fair testing.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Materials Detectives' display summarising the week's investigations.
key_questions: What material property did we test?
What was the best material for X?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided
differentiation.greater_depth: Explain testing methods and conclusions in detail independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note enquiry skills progress across the materials topic — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about materials this week with your family.
